precepts.text: Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities. For whom he did foreknow. You only have I known.
precepts.point: Moreover whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified. He shall be glorified in his Son.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” What is good about all the evil we have been watching? All of it is good, because the Lord has been warning our people, the twelve tribes, in the Bible for centuries, and we have not listened, not repented, not returned to him; we have gone into strange religions and worshipped a strange God we think is Jesus Christ. All things includes the things we think are bad for us. There is a divine purpose behind it. We are the called according to his purpose.

“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Go back to the Old Testament: who did he foreknow? Amos answers: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. For whom he did foreknow: you only have I known. The twelve tribes of Israel.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, he punished us, and the punishment itself is part of the all things that work together for good. It is his warning to return.

“he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son”. Predestinated who? The twelve tribes of Israel, whom he is transforming into the image of Christ, his Son, “that he might be the firstborn among many brethren.”

precepts.text: Can two walk together, except they be agreed? That is the answer to congregating with somebody who has been put out of the body.
precepts.point: The truth for us is the only thing we have to get up out of here. This is all we have. There is no plan B. Outside of this is death. And what God is really asking of us is a small thing in comparison to the sins that we have committed. So what is hard about not stealing, not swearing, not lying, not committing adultery, keeping the Sabbath day holy? Those are minor things. Minor, in the scope of eternal life.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” That is the answer to the one who decides not to congregate with the body on the Sabbath, or to congregate partially, and then congregates with somebody that has been put out of the body. That is out of order, and it is sin.

The Sabbath is not negotiable: remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. We cannot cook, we cannot buy, we cannot sell on the Lord's Sabbath day, and we must congregate, because it is a holy convocation. There is no way around that; you cannot decide not to do it. It is those small things, the application of God's laws, that separate us.

People do otherwise because we rationalise in our minds what we think is acceptable and what God will be all right with. God said, No, my commandments are straight; this is what I told you to do. Our biggest problem is trying to put our own thoughts in on how it should be done, but the Lord said, Your thoughts are not my thoughts. It is not hard. It only gets hard when we start to rationalise.

Imagine if that is how we started, people coming and going, this one wearing a yarmulke, this one wearing that. That is not how you build God's army. There must be structure, and the leaders are the example, the representative of what a godly Israelite looks like. When there is no agreement in the body, there is no truth in the land, and the land mourns.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.why:
“For whom he did foreknow”. Foreknow means knew from the past. Who did God know from the past? Everybody? The church? No. That has to be stressed, especially on the street, because people are so brainwashed with supersessionism, replacement theology, that they say foreknow means everybody in the church.

Amos settles it: “Hear this word that the Lord hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, You only have I known of all the families of the earth”. The family God knew is the family he brought up out of Egypt, the children of Israel. So it is no church he is talking about: no Presbyterian, no Catholic, all that garbage.

“therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities”. Because he knew us, we were punished.

Paul could have said Judah and Israel plainly, as he does in Hebrews and in Romans 9, but in many of his epistles he uses other words for the 12 tribes. “whom he did foreknow” is one of them: the 12 tribes, the only family on earth he has known.

precepts.text: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
precepts.point: After the testimony, the temple of the tabernacle of the testimony opens and seven angels come out with the seven last plagues.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
“The temple of the tabernacle of the testimony in heaven was opened”: everything the prophets wrote, the testimony, is opened, meaning we are understanding it and teaching it. Then “the seven angels came out of the temple, having the seven plagues”, and received “seven golden vials full of the wrath of God”, and a great voice said, “Go your ways, and pour out the vials of the wrath of God upon the earth.” The testimonies speak of the judgment and death that has to take place on the earth.

But before that can happen, something has to happen first. Amos reads: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” That is the lion we read in Ezra, roaring and chasing the eagle out of the wood. “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?” The trumpet is the witnesses, us teaching; when we testify, the people better be afraid. “Shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The Lord is behind it, through the angels with the seven last plagues.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The prophets are his witnesses, and the secret he reveals to them is his testimonies. And when he reveals it to us, we are supposed to testify.

“The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord God hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” The lion roaring is Christ speaking to us, and we prophesy. “Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt”: Ashdod is modern-day Tel Aviv in the land of Israel, and the land of Egypt is America. That is where we have to testify, and then the plagues are poured out.

The Bible. Whatever the scripture says, the prophecy is going to happen. Forget the dumb pastors and dumb Christians who do not know anything.

Amos shows who is behind what is happening: “Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the Lord hath not done it?” The trumpet is the Bible. And yes, there is evil in America, and the Lord has done it.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” We are the prophets. Our job, brothers, is to prepare our people for what is coming. Our job is not to pick up guns and knives thinking you can do something to the white man; this man will wipe you out just like that. Our job is to bring the people back to Messiah and prepare their minds for the second coming of Jesus Christ, the black Messiah, revealing the Bible plainly so they may repent. Wait on the Lord.

“come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.” We are Zion, and our job is to declare in Zion the work of the Lord: what is coming, and how to fix your spirit and build yourself up. To our brothers and sisters in Venezuela: repent. You cannot stop the white man; let him do what he was supposed to do. The evil in the city is the Lord’s counsel standing, and it is revealed to his prophets.

precepts.text: Surely the Lord will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
precepts.point: God reveals his secrets to his servants the prophets.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Colossians says Christ is “the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things.” He was the first thing created, before the earth, before the heavens, before the angels. God created him and told him to create everything else: the angels, stars, planets, galaxies and paradise in heaven, and a spiritual realm that cannot be seen.

Moses saw the secrets of that time, creation included, and wrote about it in a similitude, and a lot of it he hid. Those hidden things are the secrets of wisdom, and they are double: a scripture says one thing and also another thing, and when we read it again the Most High takes us to see it on another level.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” The secrets Moses hid, God reveals to His servants the prophets. Paul and the apostles understood the depth and width of the knowledge of God, because the spirit of God revealed the hidden mysteries to them. After the last of the apostles’ students died, that understanding died with them and all kinds of paganism came into the church.

But God has sent His sons back on the earth, and the proper understanding of these scriptures is coming back out. People question it when they hear that the men of IUIC are prophets. We are going to show you the secrets, and you judge for yourself.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” Noah was a preacher of righteousness, a servant of the Most High, and the Lord revealed to him what his younger son had done while he slept.

Out of that revelation came the words: “Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren”, and “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem”. It was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.” Abram was His servant, and what came to him in the deep sleep and the horror of great darkness was the Lord revealing His secret: the prophecy of what would befall his seed.

The Lord does nothing without first showing it to His prophets. The sacrifice was laid out, the sun went down, and the Most High revealed to Abram what He was about to do.

Israel is the whole family brought up out of Egypt, and the Most High says you only have I known of all the families of the earth. So all the kindreds of the earth points to the one family, Israel, that descends from Abraham, not to all nations.
